problem: Given that ${\int }_{-e}^{0}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x=A,$ what is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{e}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x?$

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x),$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x).$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. Therefore, we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Notice that $f(x)={e}^{{x}^{2}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & ={e}^{(-x)^{2}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(-x) \\  & ={e}^{{x}^{2}}(-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)) \\  & =-{e}^{{x}^{2}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x) \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)={e}^{{x}^{2}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)$ is an odd function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-\frac{\pi }{3}}^{\frac{\pi }{3}}{e}^{{x}^{2}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
